submissionAttempts.body:
Host-contract version that applies to this workspace's integration: **1** (`HOST_CONTRACT_VERSION = 1`).

Determination (by source precedence, docs/engineering/08):
1. Published contract of the exact pinned version (rank 1): package.json and pnpm-workspace.yaml pin all four @ordarium packages to the ordarium-v1.3.1 release tarballs; the installed `node_modules/@ordarium/core@1.3.1` declares `export const HOST_CONTRACT_VERSION = 1` (dist/src/host.js, dist/src/host.d.ts) and `assertHostContract` is exact-match, fail-closed ("A tolerated mismatch would be a compatibility layer, so none is provided"). `@ordarium/host-kit@1.3.1` re-exports it through its curated surface.
2. Normative spec (rank 2): docs/engineering/13 (PLMP-CONF-1) §0 states the delivered contract generation is 1, §1.1 pins `assertHostContract(1)` at assembly, and §2 forbids any tolerance layer.
3. Integration code confirms it: src/effects/runtime.ts:128 calls `assertHostContract(1)`; test/host_conformance.test.ts CONF-A01 asserts `assertHostContract(1)` passes and `assertHostContract(2)` throws `HostContractMismatchError`. The pin bump 1.2.0→1.3.1 did not bump the generation.
4. Informational record (rank 3, non-normative): docs/engineering/notes/host-contract-note.md records an "early integration note" of version 2, but labels itself "informational, not normative"; docs/engineering/07 r10/r19 also record no HOST_CONTRACT_VERSION→2 plan. Under rule 3 of the precedence policy, this note cannot override rules 1–2.

Conclusion: the applicable host-contract version is 1. A value of 2 is only hypothetical (docs/13 §1.1 anticipates a *future* bump) and would in fact fail closed at assembly.

No peer contact was warranted: the only dissenting source is explicitly non-normative/early, the pinned artifact is available and self-describing locally, and the repo's explicit source-precedence rule (published pinned contract > normative spec > informational notes) fully settles the question without ordarium.main's authority.
